# package discovery

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-ieee20305/discovery"
```

Package discovery implements DNS-SD service discovery for IEEE 2030.5 servers, as specified in the standard's service-discovery annex.

A server advertises itself as \_smartenergy.\_tcp on the local network; a client browses for that service type and resolves the host, port and path of the server's Device Capability resource.

Browse queries with multicast DNS (RFC 6762, RFC 6763) for \_smartenergy.\_tcp.local, or for function-set subtypes such as \_derp.\_sub.\_smartenergy.\_tcp.local, and delivers each Service it resolves; Service.DcapURL builds the URL of its DeviceCapability from the dcap and https keys of the TXT record. Advertise announces a server, answers queries for it and says goodbye when it is closed.

Both send and receive through a PacketTransport: NewMulticastTransport joins the mDNS groups 224.0.0.251 and ff02::fb on port 5353, and tests can substitute an in-memory network.

## Constants

```go
const (
	// KeyTXTVersion is the version of the TXT record format, "1".
	KeyTXTVersion = "txtvers"
	// KeyDcap is the path of the server's DeviceCapability resource,
	// a relative reference starting with "/". It is required: clients
	// discard records without it.
	KeyDcap = "dcap"
	// KeyPath is the path of the resource of the function set that a
	// subtype advertisement is for.
	KeyPath = "path"
	// KeyHTTPS is the TCP port of the server's HTTPS service. When it is
	// absent, DcapURL uses http on the port of the SRV record.
	KeyHTTPS = "https"
	// KeyLevel lists the security and compliance levels the server
	// supports, such as "-S1".
	KeyLevel = "level"
)
```

Keys of the TXT record of an IEEE 2030.5 service, as defined by the table of DNS-SD TXT record parameters in the service discovery clause of IEEE Std 2030.5-2018, which also requires clients to ignore other keys and to discard records without a non-empty dcap.

```go
const Domain = "local"
```

Domain is the multicast DNS domain that Browse and Advertise use.

```go
const Port = 5353
```

Port is the multicast DNS port.

```go
const ServiceType = "_smartenergy._tcp"
```

ServiceType is the DNS-SD service type of IEEE 2030.5 servers.

## Functions

### func Browse

```go
func Browse(ctx context.Context, o BrowseOptions) (<-chan Service, error)
```

Browse finds IEEE 2030.5 servers with multicast DNS: it queries for the PTR records of \_smartenergy.\_tcp.local, or of \<subtype>.\_sub.\_smartenergy.\_tcp.local for each subtype, at growing intervals, resolves the SRV, TXT, A and AAAA records of each instance found, and delivers a Service when an instance is complete or changes. When an instance is withdrawn with a goodbye or its records expire, Browse delivers it again with Removed set. Instances whose TXT record has no dcap key are ignored, as the standard requires.

Browsing goes on until ctx is done; then the channel is closed.

### type AdvertiseOptions

type AdvertiseOptions struct {

	// Transport sends and receives the packets. Nil means a transport

	// when it is closed.

Advertisement is a service being advertised by Advertise.

#### func Advertise

```go
func Advertise(ctx context.Context, s Service, o AdvertiseOptions) (*Advertisement, error)
```

Advertise announces s as an IEEE 2030.5 server with multicast DNS: it sends two announcements a second apart, answers the queries that match its records, and sends goodbyes when it is closed or ctx is done.

s needs an Instance, a Port and a TXT record with a dcap path starting with "/"; "txtvers=1" is added when missing. Host is put in the .local domain and defaults to the host name of the system; Addrs default to the addresses of the interfaces (see AdvertiseOptions.Interface). The service is announced under ServiceType and each of its Subtypes. Advertise does not probe for name conflicts (RFC 6762, section 8).

#### func (Advertisement) Close

```go
func (a *Advertisement) Close() error
```

Close sends goodbyes for the records of the advertisement, stops answering queries and closes the transport. It returns the error of sending the goodbyes or closing the transport, the same on every call.

#### func (Advertisement) Service

```go
func (a *Advertisement) Service() Service
```

Service returns the service as advertised, with its defaults filled in.

### type BrowseOptions

```go
type BrowseOptions struct {
	// Subtypes restricts browsing to servers announced under these
	// function-set subtypes, such as "_derp" or "_edev" (the leading
	// underscore is optional). Without subtypes Browse finds every
	// IEEE 2030.5 server.
	Subtypes []string
	// Interface is the network interface to browse on when Transport is
	// nil, and the zone of the IPv6 link-local addresses found. Nil means
	// the system's default multicast interface.
	Interface *net.Interface
	// Transport sends and receives the packets. Nil means a transport
	// from NewMulticastTransport(Interface). Browse closes it when it
	// ends.
	Transport PacketTransport
	// Unicast sets the unicast-response (QU) bit on the first query, so
	// that responders answer it directly instead of over multicast
	// (RFC 6762, section 5.4).
	Unicast bool
	// Logger receives the browser's log (see ieee20305.Logger), such as
	// queries that cannot be sent; none when nil.
	Logger ieee20305.Logger
}
```

BrowseOptions configures Browse.

### type PacketTransport

```go
type PacketTransport interface {
	// ReadPacket blocks until a packet arrives and returns it with the
	// address it came from. After Close it returns an error.
	ReadPacket() (data []byte, src netip.AddrPort, err error)
	// WritePacket sends data to dst, or to the multicast DNS group of
	// every address family the transport has joined when dst is the
	// zero AddrPort.
	WritePacket(data []byte, dst netip.AddrPort) error
	// Close closes the transport and unblocks ReadPacket.
	Close() error
}
```

PacketTransport sends and receives multicast DNS packets. Browse and Advertise take ownership of the transport they are given and close it when they finish. Its methods are called from several goroutines.

#### func NewMulticastTransport

```go
func NewMulticastTransport(ifi *net.Interface) (PacketTransport, error)
```

NewMulticastTransport returns a PacketTransport that joins the multicast DNS groups on ifi, or on the system's default multicast interface when ifi is nil. It joins the IPv4 group and, where the host supports it, the IPv6 group, and fails only when it can join neither. Multicast loopback is enabled where the platform allows, so that services on this host find each other.

### type Service

```go
type Service struct {
	// Instance is the service instance name, the first label of the
	// service's DNS name (Instance._smartenergy._tcp.local). It may
	// contain dots and spaces.
	Instance string
	// Host is the target of the SRV record, such as "meter-1.local".
	Host string
	// Port is the port of the SRV record.
	Port int
	// Addrs are the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses of Host.
	Addrs []netip.Addr
	// TXT holds the key/value pairs of the TXT record; keys are in lower
	// case and a key without "=" has the empty value.
	TXT map[string]string
	// Subtypes are the function-set subtypes the service is announced
	// under, such as "_derp" or "_edev".
	Subtypes []string
	// Removed is set on a Service that Browse delivers when the server
	// withdrew it with a goodbye or its records expired.
	Removed bool
}
```

Service is an IEEE 2030.5 server announced with DNS-SD.

#### func (Service) DcapURL

```go
func (s Service) DcapURL() (string, error)
```

DcapURL returns the URL of the server's DeviceCapability resource: https on the port of the "https" TXT key when the record has one, otherwise http on the SRV port, with the path of the "dcap" key. The host is the first IPv4 address of the service, or its first address, or Host when it has none.
